utterances.text: Could you tell us, how large were these areas where the clashes were occurring on both sides of the confrontation line? I wouldn't like to go into that myself. I just want your take on this. How deep on both sides of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Between a maximum of about 2.000 metres from the line where they were divided. Maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So there were units fighting in those areas, but there was no firing along the front line itself, because the forces there were separated by an area that was about 15 metres long. That's all that separated them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You go on to state that, in your opinion, the HQs of the BH army were also among the military targets, and you go on to state that these were not within the city itself; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes. The main headquarters was outside the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But the Main Staff -- you say the Main Staff of the corps, the corps HQ; is that right? It was in the city itself, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: The Sarajevo Corps headquarters was inside the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. So you suggest here that it was never hit, although the BSA were targeting it, which is hard to understand. That's what you said at the time, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: I did so, and I was surprised at the building, that it was standing absolutely intact, because you couldn't hit the -- the Serb forces couldn't hit this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But isn't that a sign that around the building there were units protecting the corps HQ? There were weapons deployed around the building and soldiers who would have constituted a military target. Wouldn't that have seemed to be the case, sir?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Any headquarters is a military target.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There's something that I've skipped. You list the Presidency, too, as a target; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The Presidency was the Supreme Command of the entire army. It was right in the middle of the city, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: It was, and I have listed it as a military target because of the same, that it was the Supreme Command of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: A military target, yes. Thank you. You go on to say, "The brigade HQ ..." When you say that, do you mean the units in the area 2 kilometres deep from the front line? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: The fighting brigade headquarters were within those 2 kilometres, or whatever it would be. These were not in civilian areas where the normal people were living.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But they were within that 2 kilometre area --

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: -- in Sarajevo; right? And the same thing applied along the entire front line, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: I suppose so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: There were brigades there in all these places, with their support units or auxiliary units. I will not be listing those now. I asked Mr. Dragomir Milosevic to tell me about those brigades. I myself served back in the military in 1969; I'm not very knowledgeable about that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not get the last part of counsel's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please repeat the question. Please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The brigades -- my apologies. Maybe I put this there so they couldn't hear. I am asking you about this: A brigade has so many people, but they have their own units. Each brigade, all of those units were deployed around the front line. I'm talking about the front line held by the BH army. All those brigades, as you have confirmed for us - this was 2 kilometres deep - so all those brigades were inside this line held by the BH army, and all over along the entire line, in all these places. Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, that is right, because the physical features on the ground, in places they had to be closer; at places they were slightly back. But they were not beyond 2.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Next you state the exit of the tunnel under the airport as a potential military target. Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that on an almost daily basis, especially during the tenure of Dragomir Milosevic, and also the time after you got there and after that, a lot of soldiers entered Sarajevo through that tunnel and would use the same tunnel to go back, to go to Igman to do something there, and new forces were being brought into Sarajevo; is that correct? Do you know anything about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: That is true, and that's why I've listed it as a military target.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: At the very end you even list the government offices, because probably there were soldiers around the government offices, too; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. An additional question: I'm moving on to Debelo Brdo now. That's the next thing I want to discuss because there were many references to Debelo Brdo in your statement. You were there, weren't you? I have no time to show you the map now. You were at Debelo Brdo in your capacity as an observer, were you not?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, I've been on Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Culina Kapa?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: No, I don't remember this name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Mojmir, which is a long ridge to the right of Debelo Brdo? And it's quite a long one, indeed.

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: I won't remember the name, but, yes, there were ridges jutting out of Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: There were BH soldiers deployed there, BH army soldiers, and the same appeared to be the case at Debelo Brdo, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: The BiH was deployed at Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me not dwell on this because there's never an end to this. From the north, I suppose you know that, because that is impossible not to see for anyone arriving in Sarajevo, Zuc and Hum, especially the hill where the TV aerial is positioned.

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All those were the positions manned by the BH army; right?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, they were manned by BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Page 7, paragraph 1, of the English version. You speak about Croats in Kiseljak here. Were you able to find it?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: No, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Page 7, in the English version, for the first paragraph. You --

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: The first paragraph, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So this is about Kiseljak. You see what you see here. "One could call it strange that the Serbs never shelled Croat areas but always Muslim areas in regions where these two factions were close together ..." Was that the case? Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: "Also, Kiseljak was never shelled." And it was Croat controlled; right?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes. During my stay it was not shelled, but earlier on Kiseljak had received shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It's an area that is not so small on the demarcation line where the Croats were, at the front line, at the demarcation line; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: No, it's an area that is not so small. Yes, the confrontation line between the Croats and the Republika Srpska was not too small, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What I want to ask you, and I hope you can give me an answer, because there were no provocations and nobody shot at each other, then naturally there were no clashes. This, perhaps, is a conclusion rather than a question, so it perhaps could not be -- I am perhaps not permitted to ask it, but perhaps I am. So, in other words, there were no clashes there because nobody fired on anyone there.

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: It may be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So now we come to Debelo Brdo. That's page 7, halfway down, a couple of paragraphs down from Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yeah, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You say here that "The Republika Srpska army attacked Sarajevo," and I want to read everything to be completely fair, "on the 16th and 17th of May to conquer Debelo Brdo from where they would be able to control the whole city centre of Sarajevo." Is that so?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes. The position dominated the city centre of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And this position that dominated the city centre of Sarajevo was held by the Bosnia-Herzegovina army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: That's correct. In this particular area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Had Serbs taken this position, as you say here, it would have been a great advantage for them at the negotiating table. This is what you say here. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: However, what I want to ask you about is the second reason. Another reason to attack this area was because the BH army snipers had, from their positions, a clear view of Grbavica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And I don't want to dwell on this. Let us move on to the next paragraph. You say: "The Bosnian Serbs wanted to have the western side of the Miljacka river." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Want I was to ask you is this: Was not their primary objective to stop the sniping incidents where Grbavica was targeted from Debelo Brdo? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: That could have been a military aim, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, slightly to the left of Debelo Brdo, below its slopes is the Jewish cemetery not located there. This is an area where both the Serbs and Bosnia-Herzegovina troops were deployed. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, I have been to the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And is it located below the slopes of the Debelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes. It is located on the slopes of Debelo Brdo and along the track which goes up to Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I hope I will be able to finish this fairly quickly. You said that when you arrived in Sarajevo on the 13th of February, 1995, that you stayed until the 19th of January, 1996.

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to go back to page 5. I'm sorry. Let me just check once again. Yes, that's correct. It is on page 5 of the English version. And please focus on the paragraph where you talk about the chronology of your tour of duty. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to find it?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to read a couple of things to you. You said that you landed on a certain date, and at that moment the Cessation of Hostilities Agreement was in effect, the COHA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I will not read the next sentence because it seems to me that it has nothing to do with Sarajevo - and the Prosecutor may not agree with me on this - but then you go on to say: "In Sarajevo there were some major agreements to be monitored, like the cease-fire, the airport agreement, the anti-sniping agreement, and the agreement on the weapon collection points." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In this regard I would like to ask you the following: The areas where the Serbs' weapons were collected, the points where the weapons would be stored were designated by the United Nations. You do know that.

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: There points were designated by the United Nations after discussion with the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And then you go on to say something about Bosnian weapons. You say that the weapons that were under the UN control, that they did not take out their weapons before June 1995, when the offensive took place. And we're talking about 100 -- in fact, this is my question to you: Do you know that there were 150 heavy artillery pieces there?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: On the Serb side or on the BiH side?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The BH army side.

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: I do not know the exact count on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But they took it out of the UNPROFOR control. It was no longer controlled by UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: After June they had taken out some weapons, in June, when they were launching an offensive, and before that they were under UN control.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. And did you know -- I cannot really go into this document because it would take us five minutes to get at the document. So if you don't know anything about it, just tell me so. You knew that, according to the reports and the assessments of the Military Intelligence Services in UNPROFOR, that the BH army, ever since December, had been actually preparing for the offensive that would be launched after the winter, or rather, in spring. Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: The speculations were there, but I cannot comment whether they were preparing for the offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let's take it one step at a time. I have to apologise. You know that there were talks, in fact, that the cease-fire agreement that was in force from January until April, that negotiations were going on to extend the agreement and that the Serbs wanted to have it extended indefinitely, and that they wanted all activities to cease in the entire territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the BH army did not want to talk about the extension of the cease-fire agreement under no conditions? They did not want to talk about the extension.

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, that is -- that is correct. The BiH army did not want to freeze on the front lines that were there. They were not satisfied with what they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You do know that the BH army -- I will try to wrap up as soon as possible, and I will actually have to forego asking some questions. You do know that the BH army, in particular its 1st Corps, had the supremacy in terms of the number of troops over the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: That is correct, that the BiH army had more numbers, but it was overcompensated by the firepower at the disposal of the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's why I'm asking you this, because on page 7, at the very bottom of the page, the last sentence here on page 7 of the English version, and then it actually runs over to the next page -- were you able to find the last sentence on page 7 of the English version --

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: -- and then it runs over. Were you able to find it?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I want to clear something up with you here. The Serbs knew that the Bosnians would dominate in number of troops. Is that what it says here? That's correct; right?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Nevertheless, although the Croats did not allow the weapons to come into Bosnia to supply the BH army, the BH army had the chance to rest and to resupply during the cease-fire. Is that what it says here? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: That's correct. They got the rest. They got the relief.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You do know that aeroplanes were used, as was the tunnel, to bring weapons, tonnes of weapons, for the BH army in this period. Or is it something that you're not aware of?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: There's no question of aeroplanes being used. The airfield was controlled by the UN, and only UN aircraft were landing there, or those aircraft of NATO and others which were permitted by the UN to land.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know anything about the aeroplanes that were able to land in Tuzla and then those supplies were able to reach Sarajevo by different routes. Well, I'm not going to go into that because I would like to complete my examination. Please look at the last sentence in this paragraph. I don't want to read it aloud now. In fact, I don't want to read the rest. In 1995 they were getting better materiel, and then you say: "The combination of the manpower and the achievement of better materiel for the BH army put the Serbs in the weaker position." Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, relatively weaker position.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And this is the point in time when the offensive was launched, the BH army offensive against the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would like to thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll be very brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The first point I forgot during my examination-in-chief was to tender the last document, Mr. President, we discussed, which was ter 269, the protest letter of Mr. -- I think signed by General Nikolai. If that could be admitted as an exhibit, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is Exhibit P87, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Brigadier, I just have a few matters to clear up. At the end you were asked about the numbers of heavy weapons and the materials, weaponry, available to the parties, and you also said that at the end of September, or in September, when the Bosnian Serb army had to pull out of Sarajevo or pull its heavy weapons out, I believe then you were able to see what heavy weaponry the Bosnian Serbs pulled out. Do you remember in terms of numbers, tanks, guns?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, it is -- we organised this pull-out. The Serbs had 54 tanks; the Bosnians had 3 tanks. The Serbs had 150 guns; the Bosnians had 7 guns. So that was the difference of materiel between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The next point I want to ask you is you were put a proposition by Mr. Tapuskovic that the Serbs were always being blamed the same day of the shelling, and you said yes. Can I ask you what the foundation was from your side to -- I'm not using the word "blame," but to put the responsibility of a shelling to the Serb side? What was the basis for your doing that?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: It was done professionally. The UNMO teams went to the spot where the shelling was done, or the firing was done. They made the analysis and reported back to my headquarters. On that basis we would convey to the -- to the concerned authorities who had, you know, overstepped ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: With respect, Brigadier, that doesn't tell us anything. It doesn't tell us -- you say it was done professionally, but that's self-serving. How was it done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the done that they went to the spot where the shelling had taken place. They would carry out a crater analysis, and that crater analysis was analysed and it gave a direction of fire and it gave a range from which direction it was fired, and we came to the conclusion who fired it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Does that answer your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The last point I wanted to ask you, Brigadier: You said there was this 2.000-meter zone around the confrontation line, and I quote you, "where these clashes were occurring." Now, are you saying that in this area there was a kind of military activity going on?

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yeah. Up to a maximum, considering the range of weapons at the disposal of the foot soldiers, it couldn't have more than 2.000 metres. That is the maximum, I said, as the area where the clashes were taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: But you agree that this did not allow to engage at civilians who might be -- happen to be in this zone defined as 2.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: Yes, I fully agree with you. You don't -- when a sniper is shooting at a child, he knows it's a child and it's not a combatant. If he's shooting at a woman, he knows she's not a combatant. So it's not difficult for people to discriminate between combatants and non-combatants.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And the last point, when you say in your witness statement - and you confirmed it in questions by the Defence - that government buildings might be military targets also because soldiers might be standing around, again, that does not allow to shoot at civilians which might be around government offices.

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: I would agree with you. It doesn't give a licence to anybody to shoot at civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And that would refer to both sniping and shelling.

utterances.speaker: GHULAM MUHAMMAD MOHATAREM
utterances.text: And shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Brigadier, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for coming to give it, and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We had anticipated that the cross-examination would have been longer. The next witness, is that witness still around or has the witness left?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, unfortunately, my e-mail is not working here, so I -- I know that when we got the guidance from the Trial Chamber at the beginning of the session, I asked that the lawyer handling the next witness inform Victim and Witnesses Unit, and my assumption is that the witness has been sent back to her hotel. But if we can have a moment, we can check to see if she's still in the building; and if she is, we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I need to investigate something further, because Mr. Tapuskovic made a --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- a submission about lateness and being informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I can address that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What that was a reference to is, when we informed counsel, Defence counsel, a month ago about who the witnesses were going to be this first week, we did not include that witness because we thought we were going to have a -- we did not know we were going to have a double session on this day. We then found out that there was going to be a double session and we were told to put -- add on another witness and we did. When we did that, however, we, just by oversight, forgot to inform Defence counsel. They only realised this yesterday; we only realised this yesterday. So what Mr. Tapuskovic -- and it was just merely an oversight on our part, and we apologise for that. What Mr. Tapuskovic referred to in terms of our agreement, which is, of course, subject to the Court's endorsement, is that we agreed that we would take the position that it would be fine for us to do the direct examination and that the cross-examination could wait until Monday so that Defence counsel is not prejudiced by our oversight. So that is what was being referred to. So I think that if the witness is here we could do the direct examination, but I don't -- the witness -- unfortunately, the witness is not here. I've just received a note that the witness is not here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, given the situation, I have nothing to add. I did have a few points, but they do not have any bearing on the merits, so I don't want to bother you with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The matter has been explained. We will adjourn until Monday, 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 22nd day of January, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.26 p.m.,
